correctness.rationale: For the specified Cauchy-invariant generalized Boole family, Cayley conjugacy gives an exact degree-two Blaschke product. Its iterated first and second Taylor coefficients determine every stated two- and three-time expectation by Haar orthogonality and analytic quotient factorization. Multiplicity counting establishes finite cumulants, and absolutely convergent geometric sums establish the asymptotic coefficient, with fixed interior parameters. The standalone verification script returned VERIFY_OK for exact rational coefficient recurrences, finite combinatorial identities, and independent finite quadrature; these tests corroborate but do not replace the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The invariant Cauchy state has undefined raw coordinate moments, making its bounded canonical Cayley-phase observable a natural object for fluctuation analysis. An exact all-horizon three-time law rather than an arbitrary numerical moment yields an all-horizon cubic cumulant and a sharp asymptotic normalization. The coefficient distinguishes two physically different approaches to nonmixing with zero Lyapunov exponent: linear suppression near alpha=0 versus quadratic explosion near alpha=1. Existing second-order/CLT theory alone does not quantify this finite-time asymmetry.
